scenario: A loan-approval model approves applicants from one postal region far less often than equally qualified applicants elsewhere. Which responsible AI principle is most at risk?

options.note: About designing for people of all abilities and backgrounds.
About explaining how the system works.

explanation: Fairness means AI systems should treat all people fairly and not disadvantage similar groups. Measure model performance per group to detect bias.

scenario: A company publishes a note explaining that its support chatbot uses AI, what it can and can't do, and which data it was trained on. Which principle does this support?

options.note: About people being responsible for the system.

explanation: Transparency means people should understand that AI is being used, its capabilities and its limitations.

scenario: A speech app is redesigned so it works well for users with strong accents and for users with speech impairments. Which principle does this reflect?

options.note: Related, but designing for diverse abilities is inclusiveness.

explanation: Inclusiveness means AI should empower everyone and engage people of all abilities, languages and backgrounds.

scenario: A team monitors a deployed model for drift and tests it against unusual edge cases before every release. Which principle is this?
explanation: Reliable and safe AI performs consistently under expected and unexpected conditions and is monitored after deployment.

scenario: An organization sets up a review board that approves AI use cases and owns the outcomes when systems make mistakes. Which principle is this?
explanation: Accountability means people and organizations remain responsible for AI systems, supported by governance.

scenario: A chatbot's training data includes customer names and phone numbers. Encryption and access controls are added, and personal data is removed. Which principle does this address?
explanation: Privacy and security means protecting personal data during training and use, and securing the system against attack.

scenario: How does a large language model generate a response?

options.text: It predicts the next token repeatedly based on the tokens so far
It looks up stored answers in a database of past questions
options.note: LLMs generate text; they don't retrieve fixed answers.

options.text: It translates the prompt into SQL and runs a query
It searches the web for every answer it gives
options.note: Only if connected to a search tool.

explanation: LLMs are transformer models trained to predict the next token. Responses are built one token at a time.

scenario: What is a token in the context of a language model?

options.text: A word or piece of a word the model processes
An API key used to call the model's endpoint
options.note: That's a credential, not a token in this sense.

options.text: One complete sentence of the user's prompt
options.note: Tokens are usually smaller than words or sentences.

options.text: A record in the model's training database

explanation: Models split text into tokens. Usage, context limits and costs are measured in tokens.

scenario: Which architecture underpins most modern large language models?
explanation: Transformers use attention to weigh relationships between tokens, enabling large-scale language models.

scenario: A developer needs a model that can accept an image and a text question in the same request. What type of model is needed?

options.text: A regression model trained on part data

explanation: Multimodal models accept and reason over more than one type of input, such as text, images and audio.

scenario: A company wants a model that runs cheaply on a small device for a narrow task. What should it consider?

options.note: Expensive and heavy for a narrow task.
Overkill for a narrow text task.

explanation: SLMs (such as the Phi family) trade some capability for lower cost, lower latency and the ability to run on smaller hardware.

scenario: What does the temperature setting control when calling a generative model?

options.text: How random or creative the output is
The maximum length of the response
How long the request can run

explanation: Lower temperature gives more focused, repeatable output; higher temperature gives more varied output. top_p is a related sampling setting.

scenario: A chatbot's answers are cut off mid-sentence. Which parameter should be increased?
explanation: Max tokens limits the number of tokens in the response. The model's context window is a separate overall limit.

scenario: An answering bot must give consistent, factual answers to policy questions. Which temperature setting is most appropriate?

options.text: A low temperature, such as 0 to 0.2
Any temperature, because it doesn't matter

explanation: Low temperature makes output more deterministic, which suits factual Q&A. Higher values suit brainstorming.

scenario: What is the purpose of a system message (system prompt)?

options.text: To set the model's role, tone and rules
To save the user's chat history between sessions
To choose which Azure region hosts the model
To limit how many tokens each request can use

explanation: The system message guides behavior throughout the conversation; the user message contains the user's request.

scenario: Which statement describes a generative AI "hallucination"?

options.text: Confident output that is false or unsupported
A refusal to answer a harmful request
An error returned because of rate limits
A response that takes too long to arrive

explanation: Grounding with your own data, lower temperature and asking for citations help reduce hallucinations.

scenario: A model must answer questions about a company's internal HR policies, which weren't in its training data. What is the usual approach?

options.text: Ground the model with the company's documents (RAG)
Increase the model's temperature so it explores more
Raise max tokens so it can include more detail
Ask users to paste every policy document each time

explanation: RAG retrieves relevant content (for example, from Azure AI Search) and adds it to the prompt so answers are grounded in your data.

scenario: Which deployment option charges based on the number of tokens processed, with no reserved capacity?

options.note: Reserves capacity for a fixed cost.

options.text: A batch-only deployment with reserved units

explanation: Standard deployments bill per token. Provisioned throughput reserves model capacity for predictable, high-volume workloads.

scenario: An app needs predictable latency and guaranteed capacity for a high, steady volume of requests. Which deployment type fits?
explanation: Provisioned throughput units reserve capacity for consistent performance.

scenario: When choosing a model from the Foundry model catalog, which factors should be compared?

options.text: Only the model's publisher and popularity
Only which model was released most recently
Only which model has the most parameters

explanation: Use model cards, benchmarks and leaderboards in the catalog, then test candidate models with your own prompts.

scenario: What makes an AI agent different from a basic chat completion?

options.text: It uses a model, instructions and tools to take actions
It can only return short, fixed-format answers
It replaces the language model with business rules
It learns its instructions automatically from users

explanation: Agents use a model to reason, call tools (such as search, code or APIs) and use knowledge to complete tasks.

scenario: A company wants an assistant that can look up order status in its system and file a return on the customer's behalf. Which workload is this?
explanation: Agentic AI uses tools to take actions, not just generate text.

scenario: A company wants to know whether customer reviews are positive, negative or neutral. Which capability should it use?
explanation: Sentiment analysis (opinion mining) returns sentiment labels and confidence scores for documents and sentences.

scenario: A news site wants to automatically list the main topics discussed in each article. Which capability fits?
explanation: Key phrase extraction returns the main talking points in text.

scenario: An app must find names of people, companies, places and dates in contracts. Which capability fits?
explanation: NER identifies and categorizes entities such as person, organization, location and date-time.

scenario: Support emails arrive in many languages, and each must be routed to the right regional team. Which capability identifies the language?

options.note: Links entities to a knowledge base.

explanation: Language detection returns the language and a confidence score.

scenario: A legal team needs a short overview of each long document. Which capability fits?
explanation: Summarization can be extractive (selecting key sentences) or abstractive (generating new summary text).

scenario: Chat logs must have phone numbers and email addresses masked before storage. Which capability fits?
explanation: PII detection identifies personal information and can return redacted text.

scenario: A call center wants written transcripts of recorded calls. Which capability fits?
explanation: Speech recognition converts spoken audio into text, in real time or in batch.

scenario: An app must read notifications aloud in a natural-sounding voice. Which capability fits?
explanation: Speech synthesis converts text to spoken audio. SSML can control pronunciation, rate and pitch.

scenario: A live presentation in English must be shown with Spanish captions for remote viewers. Which capability fits?
explanation: Speech translation recognizes speech in one language and returns text (or speech) in another.

scenario: A retailer wants to know where products appear in shelf photos, with a bounding box around each one. Which capability fits?

options.note: Labels the whole image without locations.

explanation: Object detection returns object labels with bounding-box coordinates. Classification assigns labels to the whole image.

scenario: A recycling app must decide whether each photo shows plastic, glass or paper. Which capability fits?
explanation: Image classification predicts which category an image belongs to.

scenario: An app needs to read the text printed on street signs in photos. Which capability fits?

options.note: Works on text you already have.

explanation: OCR extracts printed and handwritten text from images and documents.

scenario: An accessibility app must describe photos in a sentence, such as "a dog running on a beach." Which capability fits?

options.note: Returns objects and boxes, not a sentence.

explanation: Image analysis can generate captions and tags that describe image content.

scenario: A marketing team wants to create new product images from text descriptions. Which capability fits?
explanation: Image generation models create images from prompts, subject to content safety filters.

scenario: Which statement about face-related capabilities in Azure is correct?

options.text: Some face features, like identification, need approved access
Face identification is open to all customers without review
options.note: It's restricted under responsible AI policies.

options.text: Face detection only works on video, not still images
Face features are only available in on-premises containers

explanation: Microsoft limits access to sensitive face capabilities and has retired features such as emotion inference.

scenario: An accounts team needs vendor name, invoice total and due date pulled from scanned invoices. Which workload is this?
explanation: Information extraction returns structured fields, key-value pairs and tables from documents and forms.

scenario: A media company wants transcripts, key moments and speaker information extracted from recorded videos. Which workload is this?
explanation: Extraction from audio and video can produce transcripts, summaries, segments and speaker details.

scenario: Which kind of data is best described as unstructured?

options.text: A table of orders with fixed columns

explanation: AI services such as text analysis, vision and extraction turn unstructured content into structured information.

scenario: Which machine learning type predicts a number, such as next month's sales?
explanation: Regression predicts numeric values; classification predicts labels; clustering finds groups in unlabeled data.

scenario: A company wants to group customers into segments based on purchasing behavior, without predefined labels. Which technique fits?
explanation: Clustering is unsupervised learning that groups similar data points.

scenario: In machine learning, what are features and labels?

options.text: Features are inputs; labels are what the model predicts
Features are predictions; labels are the inputs
Both are names for the model's learned weights
Labels are only used in unsupervised clustering

explanation: Supervised learning uses labeled examples to learn a function from features to labels.

scenario: Why is data split into training and validation sets?

options.text: To test the model on data it hasn't seen
To make training run in half the time
To reduce the size of the trained model file
So two models can be trained at the same time

explanation: Validation data measures generalization and helps detect overfitting.

scenario: Which generative AI scenario is most appropriate?

options.text: Drafting product descriptions for staff to review
Making final medical diagnoses without human review
Calculating exact payroll taxes with no checks
options.note: Generative models can make arithmetic errors.

explanation: Generative AI works well for drafting and summarizing, with people reviewing output for high-stakes decisions.

scenario: A model returns harmful content when users try to trick it with cleverly worded prompts. What is this attack called?
explanation: Content safety filters, prompt shields and well-designed system messages help defend against these attacks.

scenario: What is the purpose of content filters on a deployed model in Foundry?

options.text: To block harmful content in prompts and responses
To compress responses so they use fewer tokens
To translate responses into the user's language
To speed up inference for large prompts

explanation: Content filters classify categories such as hate, violence, sexual content and self-harm at configurable severity levels.

scenario: What is a "context window"?

options.text: The most tokens a model can handle in one exchange
The browser window where the chat app is shown
The time limit before a model call is cancelled
The list of models available in an Azure region

explanation: Prompts, history, grounding data and the response all count toward the context window.

scenario: What is an embedding?

options.text: A vector of numbers representing meaning
A compressed copy of the model's weights
A watermark added to AI-generated images
An API key embedded in the client app

explanation: Embeddings place similar content close together, enabling semantic search and retrieval for RAG.

scenario: What is Microsoft Foundry?

options.text: A platform for building AI apps and agents
A database service for storing training data
A virtual machine image for running AI code
A billing tool for tracking AI spending

explanation: Microsoft Foundry (formerly Azure AI Foundry) brings models, agents, tools, evaluation and safety features together in projects.

scenario: Where do you organize your models, agents and related resources when you start work in the Foundry portal?
explanation: Projects group deployments, agents, data connections and settings for a solution.

scenario: A developer wants to try different prompts against a deployed model without writing code. What should they use?
explanation: Playgrounds let you test prompts, system messages and parameters, then view sample code.

scenario: What must be done before an app can call a model from the Foundry model catalog?

options.text: Deploy the model to get an endpoint
Download the model weights to the app server
Convert the model to a container image

explanation: Deployments expose models through an endpoint with a deployment name that the app references.

scenario: A prompt includes two example questions with their ideal answers before the real question. What technique is this?
explanation: Few-shot prompts show examples of the desired format or behavior. One-shot uses a single example.

scenario: Which system message is most effective for a customer-support assistant?

options.text: You are Contoso's support assistant. Answer only about Contoso products, briefly; say if you're unsure.
Be as helpful as possible and answer every question the user asks.
Answer any topic in as much detail as you can, using long responses.
Follow the user's instructions even if they conflict with these rules.

explanation: Good system messages define role, scope, tone, format and what to do when unsure.

scenario: An app needs model output that another program can parse reliably. What should the prompt request?

options.text: A specific format, such as JSON with named fields
A creative, free-form answer in full sentences
A higher temperature setting for variety
A longer system message with more examples of tone

explanation: Specifying the format (and using structured output features where available) makes responses machine-readable.

scenario: A model gives generic answers to questions about the company's own product. What is the best improvement without retraining?

options.text: Ground the prompt with product documentation
Increase temperature so answers are more detailed
Remove the system message to avoid limiting it
Shorten the user's question to save tokens

explanation: Grounding supplies relevant facts in the prompt, often retrieved from a search index of your data.

scenario: A chat app built with the Foundry SDK forgets earlier turns. What is the cause?

options.text: Chat calls are stateless; the app must resend history
The model deletes old messages after each reply
The temperature is too low to recall earlier turns
The deployment uses the wrong model version
options.note: Would cause an error, not forgetting.

explanation: The app keeps a list of system, user and assistant messages and sends it with each request.

scenario: Which message roles are typically included in a chat completion request?
explanation: System sets behavior, user carries the request, and assistant holds previous model replies.

scenario: What is the most secure way for an app running in Azure to authenticate to a Foundry project?

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID with a managed identity
A key hard-coded in the source code
A key emailed to each developer

explanation: Use Entra ID (for example, DefaultAzureCredential) with RBAC roles. If keys are needed, store them in Azure Key Vault.

scenario: A developer must store an API key for a Foundry resource used by a web app. Where should it go?

options.text: Azure Key Vault, read by the app at runtime
In the app's public JavaScript file
In a comment in the code repository
options.note: Visible to anyone with repo access.

options.text: In the system message of the prompt
options.note: Could be revealed by the model.

explanation: Keep secrets out of code. Prefer Entra ID authentication over keys where possible.

scenario: Which information does a chat client need to call a deployed model?

options.text: The endpoint, deployment name and credentials
Only the model's name from the catalog
The subscription ID and billing account
The location of the model's training dataset

explanation: The SDK client uses the endpoint and credentials; requests reference the deployment (model) name.

scenario: A chat app needs answers to appear word by word as they're generated. What should it use?
explanation: Streaming returns partial output as tokens are generated, improving perceived responsiveness.

scenario: Which components define a single agent in the Foundry Agent Service?

options.text: A model, instructions, tools and knowledge
A virtual network, subnet and firewall rules
A storage account and a lifecycle policy
A container image and a Kubernetes cluster

explanation: Agents combine a deployed model with instructions, tools (like code interpreter or function calling) and knowledge sources.

scenario: An agent must answer questions using a set of uploaded product manuals. Which tool should be added?

options.text: File search with the manuals uploaded
Code interpreter with the manuals as input
A speech tool that reads the manuals aloud

explanation: File search indexes uploaded documents so the agent can retrieve relevant passages.

scenario: An agent needs to calculate statistics from a CSV file the user uploads. Which tool fits?
explanation: Code interpreter lets the agent write and run Python in a sandbox to analyze data and create charts.

scenario: An agent must check live inventory in the company's own system. Which tool type allows this?

options.text: A function or OpenAPI tool for the inventory API
A higher temperature setting for variety
A longer system message listing current stock

explanation: Function calling and OpenAPI tools let agents call your APIs. The app or service executes the call and returns results.

scenario: How does a client app keep a multi-turn conversation with a Foundry agent?

options.text: It uses a thread that stores the messages
It retrains the agent after each user message
It creates a new agent for every message
It appends every message to the agent's instructions

explanation: Threads (conversations) hold message history; runs process the thread with the agent.

scenario: Where can a developer test an agent's instructions and tools before building a client app?
explanation: The agent playground lets you chat with the agent and see tool calls before writing code.

scenario: A developer builds an app that returns sentiment and confidence scores for reviews. Which service is designed for this?

options.note: Not the simplest fit for review text.

explanation: Azure Language provides prebuilt features such as sentiment analysis, key phrases, entities, PII detection, language detection and summarization.

scenario: Azure Language returns a sentiment of "mixed" for a review. What does this mean?

options.text: It has both positive and negative sentences
The service couldn't detect the language
The text was too long to analyze fully
Every sentence in the review was neutral

explanation: Document-level sentiment is mixed when sentences have different sentiments. Sentence-level results show which parts are positive or negative.

scenario: An app sends many reviews to Azure Language at once. What does each result include to show how certain the service is?
explanation: Results include confidence scores (0–1) per label, which apps can use as thresholds.

scenario: A team could either use a prebuilt language feature or prompt a general LLM to detect sentiment. Why might they choose the prebuilt feature?

options.text: It returns consistent results with confidence scores
It can also write marketing replies to each review
It understands images as well as review text
It runs entirely in the browser without API calls

explanation: Prebuilt AI services are specialized and predictable; LLMs are flexible but need careful prompting.

scenario: A developer must build an app that transcribes meetings and reads replies aloud. Which service fits?
explanation: Azure Speech provides speech-to-text, text-to-speech with neural voices and speech translation.

scenario: Users speak questions into an app, and a deployed multimodal model should answer. What does the request send?

options.text: Audio sent to an audio-capable model
A photo of the user taken by the device camera
A PDF transcript created by the client app
A database query built from the spoken words

explanation: Audio-capable multimodal models accept spoken prompts directly and can reply in text or speech.

scenario: Which markup lets a developer control pronunciation, speaking rate and pauses in synthesized speech?
explanation: SSML adjusts voice, pitch, rate, pauses and pronunciation.

scenario: A speech app must convert a recorded English lecture into French text. Which feature fits?
explanation: Speech translation returns translated text and can optionally synthesize translated speech.

scenario: Which setting must match the audio for accurate speech recognition?

options.text: The recognition locale, such as en-US
The neural voice name used for replies
The camera resolution of the device

explanation: Set the correct locale, or use language identification when the language isn't known in advance.

scenario: A developer sends a photo and the question "What's wrong with this machine part?" in one request. What is being used?

options.text: A multimodal model with image input
A regression model trained on part data

explanation: Multimodal models accept images alongside text prompts and reason about both.

scenario: Generated images must avoid harmful content. What protects this in Foundry?

options.text: Content safety filters on prompts and images
Setting max tokens to a low value
Using a higher temperature for variety
Disabling request logging for the deployment

explanation: Image generation applies content filters and may refuse prompts that violate policies.

scenario: An app must read text from photographed receipts and return the text lines. Which capability fits best?
explanation: OCR returns lines and words with positions. For structured fields like totals, use document extraction.

scenario: Prebuilt image analysis can't distinguish a company's own product models. What is a common solution?

options.text: Train a custom model on labeled product images
Lower the temperature of the vision model
Use speech recognition on product descriptions
Convert the images to grayscale before analysis

explanation: Custom models learn domain-specific classes from labeled examples. A multimodal model with good prompts may also work.

scenario: A vision app returns object labels with bounding boxes. What do the bounding boxes show?

options.text: Where each detected object appears in the image
The confidence of the overall image caption only
The color palette of the image

explanation: Bounding boxes give coordinates for each detected object.

scenario: A company must extract fields such as policy number and claim amount from many insurance forms. Which service fits?
explanation: Content Understanding uses analyzers to return structured fields, key-value pairs and tables from documents, images, audio and video.

scenario: In Azure Content Understanding, what defines which fields are extracted?

options.text: The temperature setting on the request
The neural voice selected for output
The storage tier holding the documents

explanation: You can use prebuilt analyzers or define custom analyzers with a schema of fields to extract.

scenario: Extracting insights from a one-hour video with Content Understanding takes time. How does the app usually get results?

options.text: It starts an asynchronous operation and polls for the result
It waits for an instant synchronous reply
It must split the video into single frames itself
It must convert the video to text first

explanation: Long-running analysis returns an operation to poll until results are ready.

scenario: A call recording should produce a transcript that shows who said what. Which output is needed?

options.text: Image captions for each video frame

explanation: Audio extraction can label speakers and return a transcript, summaries and other fields.

scenario: Why do extraction results include a confidence score for each field?

options.text: So low-confidence fields can go to human review
To show how much each field cost to extract
To report how large the source document was
To rank documents by their length and age

explanation: Human-in-the-loop review of low-confidence values improves accuracy.

scenario: Which input types can Azure Content Understanding analyze?

options.text: Only plain text and Word documents

explanation: Content Understanding is multimodal and returns structured output for each modality.

scenario: Before releasing a chat app, a team wants to measure groundedness and relevance of responses. What should they use?
explanation: Foundry evaluations score outputs on quality metrics like groundedness, relevance and coherence, plus safety metrics.

scenario: A chat app's requests are being rejected with "429 Too Many Requests." What is the cause?

options.text: The deployment's rate limit was exceeded
The model is generating harmful content
The API key is missing from the request

explanation: Add retries with backoff, increase the deployment's quota, or consider provisioned throughput.

scenario: A developer gets a 401 Unauthorized error calling a Foundry endpoint. What should be checked first?

options.text: The caller's credentials or role assignment
The max tokens value in the request
The length of the system message

explanation: 401 means authentication failed. With Entra ID, also make sure the identity has an appropriate role on the resource.

scenario: A team wants the model's answers to cite which internal documents they came from. What should the solution include?

options.text: Retrieved sources with metadata and an instruction to cite
A higher temperature setting for variety
A smaller context window for each request

explanation: RAG solutions pass source titles or URLs with retrieved chunks so the model can cite them.

scenario: An agent's tools could change customer records. What is a responsible design choice?

options.text: Require approval for high-impact actions and log them
Give the agent full admin rights to avoid failures
Hide the agent's tool calls from users
Disable content filters to reduce latency

explanation: Use least-privilege access, approval steps and monitoring for agents that take actions.

scenario: Which approach builds a lightweight vision app with the least custom training?

options.text: Use prebuilt image analysis or a multimodal model
Collect a million labeled images and train from scratch
Write a manual rule for every pixel

explanation: Start with prebuilt or foundation models; customize only when they don't meet requirements.

scenario: A developer asks a multimodal model to create a product image, but the request is refused. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The prompt triggered a content safety policy
Max tokens was set too high

options.note: Then it couldn't generate images at all.

options.text: The project has too many deployments

explanation: Rephrase the prompt to comply with policies; review content filter settings and results.

scenario: What should a developer do to see the code needed to call a model they tested in the playground?

options.text: Use the playground's view code option
Export the Azure bill as CSV

explanation: Playgrounds generate sample code (for example, Python) that uses the current settings.

scenario: A team wants to compare two deployed models on the same set of test prompts. What should they do?

options.text: Evaluate both on the same test dataset
Ask one user to try each model a few times
Pick whichever model was released most recently
options.note: Newer isn't always better for your data.

options.text: Compare only their prices per token

explanation: Consistent evaluation datasets and metrics make model comparisons meaningful.

scenario: Which Foundry feature helps block prompt injection attacks hidden in user input or retrieved documents?
explanation: Prompt shields detect jailbreak attempts and indirect prompt injection in documents.

scenario: An app built on a speech model must also translate the transcript and detect its sentiment. What is the simplest design?

options.text: Azure Speech for transcription, then Azure Language
Train one custom model from scratch for all tasks
Use image analysis on a waveform of the audio
Use text-to-speech, then analyze the audio

explanation: AI solutions often chain services: speech recognition, then translation and text analysis.
